claims.object_text: an essential DNA end-processing enzyme in mammals with 3'-phosphatase and 5'-kinase activities; plays a pivotal role in multiple DNA repair pathways
claims.quote: Polynucleotide kinase 3'-phosphatase (PNKP), an essential DNA end-processing enzyme in mammals with 3'-phosphatase and 5'-kinase activities, plays a pivotal role in multiple DNA repair pathways.
mutation at a conserved glutamine (Gln) in PNKP leads to late-onset ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 4 (AOA4) in humans
the enzymatic activities of the mutant versus WT PNKP are comparable

claims.object_text: DNA double-strand break accumulation and activation of the DNA damage response
claims.quote: cells expressing mutant PNKP and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of AOA4 patients showed a significant amount of DNA double-strand break accumulation and consequent activation of the DNA damage response.

claims.object_text: nuclear localization severely abrogated; mutant proteins remain primarily in the cytoplasm
claims.quote: the nuclear localization of mutant PNKP is severely abrogated, and the mutant proteins remain primarily in the cytoplasm.

claims.object_text: mutated PNKP predominantly in the cytoplasm (patient PBMCs)
claims.quote: Western blot analysis of AOA4 patient-derived PBMCs also revealed the presence of mutated PNKP predominantly in the cytoplasm.

claims.object_text: impeded interaction with importin alpha but not with importin beta
claims.quote: mutation at a conserved Gln residue impedes the interaction of PNKP with importin alpha but not with importin beta

claims.object_text: absence of nuclear PNKP leads to persistent double-strand breaks, activation of the DNA damage response, and death of vulnerable brain cells (potential cause of neurodegeneration in AOA4)
claims.quote: the absence of PNKP in the nucleus leads to constant activation of the DNA damage response due to persistent accumulation of double-strand breaks in the mutant cells, triggering death of vulnerable brain cells-a potential cause of neurodegeneration in AOA4 patients.
